subject: Logic
title: Simpson's Paradox
description: A quick win: understand Simpson's Paradox.

hook.text: Hospital A is better for both mild and severe cases. Yet overall, Hospital B has better outcomes. How?

buildup.text: Simpson's paradox occurs when a trend in grouped data reverses when the groups are combined.

discovery.text: Hospital B gets more mild cases, inflating its overall number. Grouping masks the real story.

twist.text: UC Berkeley was sued for gender bias in admissions. Department-level data showed the opposite.

climax.text: Always ask: is this data hiding subgroups that could reverse the conclusion?

punchline.text: Totals can lie about the parts.
